conflicts.resolution: The brief's 'Kael Draven' collides with Kael Marren (merged draft). The Myth of the Stones character is renamed Torin Draven; the Rise of Aries journeyman Draven became Brannock.
Elias Veyron is renamed Elian Veyron (decided 2026-11-07 under the founder's delegation). Elias Mercer keeps his name.
Shared surname Ardent. Treated as one lineage: Juno is Nadia's descendant, a deliberate Convergence link.
The AI chose the name ORION after the Sagittarius regent whose fall the ancient signal records. A deliberate echo, to be revealed in The Fall of Orion and The Omega Protocol.
Ares Valorian is the first Regent of Aries (Age IV), named for the god in honour. Present-day Aries is Kael Marren. The god Ares is unrelated to Valorian's person.
The Taurus leader Tharion Voss is renamed Tharion Vorne (decided 2026-11-07 under delegation). Kaelen Voss keeps his name.
The brief says 9.17 Hz. The repository's established value is 9.1717 Hz (media.html, omega-canon.js). Canon is 9.1717 Hz everywhere.

The three principles are domains of the nine elements: Matter (Metal, Sand, Water), Energy (Fire, Wind), Consciousness (Soul); Space, Void and The All are the conditions that frame them. Proposed, needs founder approval.

The seven stones are a mortal taxonomy: the guardians sorted the nine elements into seven aspects (Creation, Memory, Time, Energy, Matter, Consciousness, Balance). The mismatch is intentional and part of the mystery.
The merged saga runs 2026-2037 (Age VI-VII). Age IV is the First War that the Solar Accord paused twelve thousand years ago, so The Rise of Aries (2026) is the Accord's test, not the First War.
'The Rise of Aries' already exists as a 2026 screenplay. Valorian's ancient rebellion becomes a flashback and a possible prequel, not a second film of the same name.

The feature film is retitled THE THIRTEENTH SEAT (decided 2026-11-07 under delegation); its id keeps the stable slug. The live micro-series keeps THE TWELVE HOUSES. The old title is kept as formerTitle.
The disappearances belong to Age III but the expeditions are modern, so pharaohs and the twelve-thousand-year Accord do not clash.
The Galactic Universe runs on its own clock and meets the others at saga chapter 11; Age V is not a human prehistory.

Work proceeds in waves, one franchise vertical at a time (screenplay, season bible, game design document, prototype), each recorded in OMEGA_STUDIOS_MASTER_STATUS.md. The totals (26 films, about 150 episodes, 4 games) stay the target, not a claim.
Shared surname Vale is by design: mother and son.
The Seven Stones shows a nine-ring wall with seven rings inscribed and two blank, seeding the nine-element canon (C-09) without naming the missing two.
The phrase 'hold the other end' appears in The Seven Stones (Ithren) and The Rise of Aries (Solenne). Treated as a deliberate cross-franchise echo and a Convergence motif.

Season 1 of The Chronicles of the Guardians runs in the eleven months before The Seven Stones and ends on the film's first present-day scene, so it keeps the brief's episode titles without retelling the film. Season 2 follows the film.

The brief's third-person open-world RPG is a design target; the first buildable artefact is a 2D top-down Vertical Slice 0, labelled PROTOTYPE until it meets the release criteria in the GDD. Multiplayer is UNAVAILABLE.

The Season 1 episode 1 beat sheet says two niches are filled in Malachar's sanctum, but Continuity Lock 1 says he holds only the Time stone until episode 6 (Energy arrives then). The episode 1 script shows one filled niche (Time) and six empty.

The Season 1 bible (Continuity Lock 8) said Torin joined the Wardens at 22 and 'fell out' twenty years before the film. The film makes him 42 and a Warden who fell out twenty years ago, so he cannot have joined at 22. Resolved while scripting episode 105: Malachar places him with the Wardens at 18 and the council expels him at 22; Perrin Hask alone keeps faith with him.

The Season 1 bible had the Lamp whisper to Torin in episode 5, but Continuity Lock 7 says the Lamp has spoken to no one but Seraphine in ninety years. Resolved in episode 105: the Warden key Torin takes carries his spoken word to the Citadel, and the Lamp tells Seraphine.

The registry says Zodiac Wars: Bloodlines is 4 seasons of 8 episodes; the Zodiac Wars canon draft and the Rise of Aries package describe a ten-episode limited series ('Season 1 opens on the Soul door') and a five-season series. Decision under delegation: keep the registry's 4 x 8, with one forgotten guardian and three Houses per season (Season 1: Soul with Aries, Libra and Pisces). The ten-episode limited series and a fifth, Null season are not adopted. The live micro-series The Twelve Houses is a separate product.

The registry gave The Human Frontier's series, Survivors of Tomorrow, no season or episode counts. Decision under delegation: 2 seasons of 8 episodes, with Season 1 (Ration Day) set in the Last City. The registry also named no characters for this franchise, so Ines Calloway, Tobias Wren and Marguerite Osei are new, proposed names.

The brief gives the surname Ardent to Nadia Ardent (The Lost Civilizations) and Juno Ardent (The Last Galactic Empire). Decision: no relation is implied in either series; a shared family is a Convergence-level reveal and must be earned by both franchises first.
